correctness.rationale: For integer m>=1, centrally symmetric full-dimensional B⊂R^m and t∈[0,1], the horizontal slices of F_t(B) have radius r(z)=1-(1-t)z. A reflected core centered at (x,c) has slice r(z)B∩(2x+r(2c-z)B). By nesting concentric homothetic B, each slice is bounded by min(r(z),r(2c-z))^m vol(B) and the bound is attained at x=0. At z=c any x≠0 strictly loses volume over a neighborhood, establishing uniqueness of horizontal center. Reflecting heights reduces optimal volume to I(c)=2vol(B)∫_c^{2c}r(u)^m du for c<=1/2 or 2vol(B)∫_c^1 r(u)^m du for c>=1/2; derivative for c<1/2 has sign 2r(2c)^m-r(c)^m, and I decreases for c>1/2. The unique interior optimum solves r(c)/r(2c)=2^(1/m), giving c=(q-1)/[(1-t)(2q-1)] until t_m=(2q-1)^-1; otherwise c=1/2. Exact volume denominator vol(B)(1-t^(m+1))/[(m+1)(1-t)] leads to both advertised core-ratio formulas. Monotone-likelihood ordering of slice-height densities proves strict increase in t on the second branch; direct denominator comparison does so on first. t=0 cone and t=1 prism boundary included. High-dimensional t=1-τ/m yields the stated crossover at τ=2ln2. Independently optimized 20 (m,t) scalar integral instances for m=1,2,7,15 against the claimed center and fraction, center error <3e-5 and volume error <1e-7. The all-base proof is analytical.

value.rationale: The Kovner–Besicovitch reflected-core fraction is an established natural affine invariant of convex geometry. Exact shape-independent optimization for arbitrary centrally symmetric bases, a unique-center phase transition, and a noncommuting large-dimensional boundary layer give substantial structure beyond classical triangle/pyramid endpoints or a numerical example.

limitations: No asymmetric base, nonhomothetic section, or measured-noisy core recovery.
